result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the differences between rasterizers and give similar fixes. A contradicts itself: it says `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased` makes Mac text thinner, then says removing it brings Mac rendering closer to Windows, when removing it actually widens the gap. B gets this right, names Windows at 100% scaling as a test target, and is shorter with less jargon, though A says more plainly that identical rendering across platforms isn't possible. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the rendering pipeline well and give the same core fixes: use a heavier weight, a larger size, better-hinted fonts, and testing on low-density screens. B adds useful points about text contrast and says plainly that identical rendering is impossible. But it contradicts itself on `-webkit-font-smoothing`: it says `antialiased` makes Mac text thinner, then claims removing it brings the Mac closer to Windows, when removing it actually widens the gap. B also leans on jargon like fpgm/prep tables that a non-specialist can't use. A is accurate, more concise, and explicitly mentions Windows at 100% scaling, though it says 'mid-range' rather than older Android.
